model
old_prose: Betrayal shatters the foundation of trust upon which we build our sense of self. It undermines our perception of reality, leaving us questioning our judgment, intuition, and even our worthiness of loyalty. This erosion of trust can destabilize our identity, forcing a painful re-evaluation of who we are, who we thought others were, and how we navigate relationships moving forward.

model
old_prose: Yes, something can be beautiful despite being morally objectionable. Beauty is a subjective and separate aesthetic experience from morality. A work of art, for example, might possess striking beauty while simultaneously depicting or exploring morally reprehensible themes. The beauty doesn't negate the moral concerns, but acknowledges a distinct, often complex, human response.
